body:
Escalation from issue-worker-high: this issue is larger than effort:high. I did not claim it, did not make a branch and did not change code.

What I found on main (b8e4d8294):

1. The 3D Finish waterline (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/rings.rs`, `waterline`) uses a ball-only "forbidden centers" law (`finishing3d/mod.rs`). The support function per facet is `q_xy·u + sqrt(r² − (cz − q_z)²)`. A flat or bull-nose tool needs a different support function. For a flat tool the facet is clipped to `z ≥ tip` and grown by R. For a bull nose the term is `(R − rc) + rho(q_z)`, with `rho` constant above the corner. The filled tool is convex, so the per-facet section stays convex, but the edge stationary points change. This is a new geometry derivation.
2. The 3D Finish verdict is law (f) (`crates/sim/src/verify/finish.rs`). It calls `stock_sim::envelope_scan` (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan.rs`), which measures a swept SPHERE (tip lifted by r). Its gouge and rest numbers are wrong for a flat or bull-nose cutter. A flat or bull-nose envelope scan needs a new distance law (triangle to cylinder or torus). This is a collision law, and the "verify reports the concave-fillet rest" item of "Done means" needs it.
3. `KindInfo` sets `tool_kinds` and the verify `Mode` per kind (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`, Finish3D: `tk::BALL`, `Mode::Envelope`). If 3D Finish takes flat tools, every non-waterline pattern must refuse them by name, and the verify mode must follow the tool. A separate "3D Contour" kind is the alternative, but it still needs items 1 and 2.

A possible short path: the 3D Pocket level law (`crates/motion/src/machining3d/mod.rs`, `cut_target(z) = footprint ∖ (slice ∪ shadow_down)`) is exact for a flat cylinder and conservative for a bull nose. Its wall ring at each level is a flat-tool waterline. But the verify part and the rest report still need new laws.

These items are new algorithms and a collision law. By the AGENTS.md effort table this is effort:max. I changed the label from effort:high to effort:max.
